texts: good. the salt-bloom store, its Cauldron Hall location, the ten-week quantity of winter supply, the past tense and the one-day gap to the autumn equinox all come through, and the holding parses as a normal event with the store as the holder. 'the late summer of Year 1' lands as a season symbol beside the year term, which is an improvisation on our side, but nothing in your sentence is lost.

mixed: the reporting event, Hesper as the reporter, the Council as the addressee and the sealed claim that the harvest had been thin are all carried, but 'previous' is silently dropped — nothing inside a reported that-clause can carry a before/after ordering, so the parse never records which new-moon harvest is meant. Assert that ordering in its own clause outside the report: "The new-moon harvest came before the autumn equinox. Hesper reported to the Council that the new-moon harvest had been thin."
